# Two README claims, checked against the repository

Repository https://github.com/ai/nanoid, commit `055d1700cc67ac843e3efb5235d806b419ec7b2b` (2026-11-05).

| claim in README.md | checked against | result | detail |
|---|---|---|---|
| No dependencies | package.json | inside | package.json: 0 dependencies, 0 peerDependencies, 0 optionalDependencies against 0 claimed |
| 117 bytes (minified and brotlied) | the size limit in package.json | inside | README 117, enforced limit 117 |
| 117 bytes, as a measurement | nothing: no measurement was recorded | cannot-assess | the run did not install or execute the project's build tools |

Both laws here are checked by a script, not by a proof assistant, and each record says so.

steps.out:
initialised  .delphi
project      nanoid
store        .delphi/store/nodes.jsonl  (append-only, one record per line, commit it)
method       .delphi/BEST_PRACTICES.md  (generated; regenerate with `delphi best-practices`)
graph        .delphi/graph/index.html   (rewritten after every mint, private to this project)
laws         .delphi/laws/              (put your Lean files here)

Next: record the source of one number you already rely on.
  delphi evidence --kind doi --ref <doi> --quote "<the words it prints>" --where "<table or section>"

Lean files are checked in your own Lake project, found from the file, so they see your
toolchain and your libraries. With no Lean on this machine, `delphi law --lean` is refused
as unchecked, never passed. A law given with --script says on its record that a script
checked it.
